sentences.text: Misc. Appeal No. 3782 of 2023

Wd. Asha Mishra And Others
 Versus
 Manish Kumar Sahu And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Arubendra Singh Parihar - Advocate for the appellan
 Shri Shailesh Kumar Mishra - Advocate for the respondent

Order 
This present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 26.04.2023, passed in MVC No.400202/2016 by VII MACT, Rewa, District Rewa.
By the said award, learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim case and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.14,54,080/- along with the interest of 10% per annum.

2. Factual matrix of the case are that on 28.02.2016, deceased Raghvendra Prasad Mishra aged 45 years, met with an accident as a result of which, the deceased sustained fatal injury and he succumbed on the spot.
The claimant filed a claim petition claiming a compensation of Rs.24,76,000/-.

Thus, the Claim Tribunal found that the accident was caused by the respondent No.1 (Driver) due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which was insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.

3. Learned MACT partly allowed the claim petition and awarded Rs.7,87,500/- under the head of "loss of dependency", Rs.2,20,000/- under the head "loss of consortium", Rs.16,500/- under the head of "funeral" and Rs.16,500 for "loss of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55380 2 MA-3782-2023 State".

Thus in total, learned MACT awarded Rs.10,24,000/- was awarded as against claim of Rs.24,76,000/-
4.
It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was responsible for causing the accident and the vehicle was insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not ?.
5. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: After going through the record and hearing the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, I find that Tribunal has awarded lower side amount under various heads.
7. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, income of the deceased instead of Rs.5,000/-, instead of Rs.6,575/- as per the collectorate guidelines.
The accident has been occurred on 28.02.2016, at that time the deceased has crossed the age of 45 years.

The monthly income of the deceased is rs.6,575/- instead of Rs.5,000/- after calculating the future prospects of 25% as per the law laid down in by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 4 ACJ 270, it should be Rs.8,218/- per month after deducting 1/4, it should be Rs.6,168/- and the yearly income would be Rs.73,968/- as per the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation &
Others reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the factor of 14 is applied looking towards the age of deceased,
it would be Rs.10,35,562/- for ''loss of dependency'' instead of Rs.7,87,500/- and the Tribunal has assessed the proper in the other heads, there is no need to interfere in that part of award.

the claimant is entitled to Rs.2,48,062/- in the 'head of loss of dependency'.

The enhanced amount shall NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55380 3 MA-3782-2023 carry the interest 6%
per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition.
8. In view of the foregoing discussion, appeal stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-
"i. The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.
vi No order as to costs."

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE DevS Wd. Asha Mishra vs Manish Kumar Sahu on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38991998/
